title: Wings — Inboard Flap Track No. 2 Rib Attachment — Eddy Current Inspection of the Rear Spar Boom

ata.title: Wing Trailing Edge — Flap Support Structure

abstract: Mandatory eddy current inspection of the inboard flap track number two rib attachment holes and the adjacent rear spar boom, required before the reinforced rib can be installed and repeated until it is.

sections.planning_reason: Elongated attachment holes and fretting product have been found at the inboard flap track number two rib on aircraft in high-cycle short-sector operation, with twenty-four findings recorded between 2015 and 2018 and the earliest at 21000 flight cycles. Two aircraft required an oversize repair of the rear spar boom. A hole that has already elongated cannot accept the reinforced rib without a repair, so the attachment must be inspected before the modification and repeatedly until it is embodied.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives an eddy current inspection of the five attachment holes of the inboard flap track number two rib and of the adjacent rear spar boom land, together with a measurement of hole ovality. It defines the acceptance criteria, the reporting requirement and the repeat interval that applies until the reinforced rib is installed.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Extend the flaps to the maintenance position and support them. Open the trailing edge access panels in zones 525 and 624. Remove the attachment bolts from the flap support rib. Clean the holes and measure the ovality with the go and no-go gauge supplied with the tool kit. Calibrate the eddy current equipment on the reference block and scan each hole and the surrounding spar boom land. An ovality above 0.15 millimetres or any crack indication makes the attachment unserviceable and must be reported to Aeralis before further flight. Where the attachment is serviceable, install new barrel nuts AGS934342-5A, re-torque the bolts and apply the corrosion inhibiting compound. Close the access panels, retract the flaps and do the flap operational test. Record the inspection and repeat it every 6000 flight cycles until the reinforced rib bulletin is embodied.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft in the MSN range Z01080 to Z09673 that are not yet at the reinforced rib standard. One aircraft is excluded because it was withdrawn from service before the effective date. Aircraft built after the production cut-in of the reinforced rib are not affected.
sections.material_note: No kit is required. Barrel nuts are consumed at each inspection and must be ordered separately; they have a four-week lead time. This bulletin is an inspection only and carries no weight change; the mass increase is recorded against the reinforcement bulletin.

type_data.compliance_time: Before the accumulation of 22000 flight cycles, or within 1200 flight cycles after the effective date of the airworthiness directive, whichever occurs later; thereafter every 6000 flight cycles.

tooling: Eddy current bolt hole probe, 4 mm
